title: Production AI Development in Python
summary: Turn a notebook prototype into a typed, testable, bounded application core.
outcomes: Define trust and adapter boundaries
Enforce authorization and deadlines
Evaluate deterministic invariants

title: Cloud and Distributed AI Systems
summary: Design idempotent asynchronous AI workloads and choose AWS compute, messaging, state, and recovery patterns from evidence.
outcomes: Model partial failure and unknown outcomes
Prove idempotency, bounded retry, and version safety
Compare AWS deployment options with capacity and operability evidence

title: Enterprise Identity and Agent Authorization
summary: Build issuer-scoped identity, default-deny policy, attenuated delegation, and exact single-use approval controls for AI tools.
outcomes: Validate token, subject, actor, tenant, and resource boundaries
Attenuate delegated authority without role or parameter injection
Prove approval binding, replay safety, and lifecycle invalidation

title: Production RAG and Knowledge Systems
summary: Build a versioned knowledge lifecycle with authorization-before-ranking, hybrid retrieval, provenance-bound citations, and measurable freshness and safety.
outcomes: Design idempotent ingestion, provenance, versioning, deletion, and poison recovery
Compare sparse, dense, hybrid, and reranked retrieval on labelled access-aware cases
Prove citation support and measure retrieval quality, forbidden outcomes, and stale exposure

title: Agentic AI Architecture and AgentCore
summary: Compare a deterministic workflow with a bounded agent through one governed tool, approval, budget, checkpoint, and recovery boundary.
outcomes: Choose the least-autonomous architecture from measured task, safety, latency, and cost evidence
Implement typed tools, current authorization, budgets, approvals, idempotency, and application-owned termination
Recover safely from timeout, cancellation, restart, duplicate delivery, stale state, and unknown effects
Map custom orchestration responsibilities to current Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capabilities

title: Model Gateways and Inference Economics
summary: Build a governed model-access boundary and compare direct, cascade, fallback, cache, and hedge policies using quality, latency, reliability, privacy, and complete cost evidence.
outcomes: Normalize provider contracts without erasing capability, safety, streaming, retention, or schema differences
Enforce authenticated model eligibility, residency, versions, hard budgets, quotas, retry classes, and validated cache scope
Measure quality-latency-cost frontiers and select a route by cost per successful compliant task
Diagnose router drift, correlated failure, silent fallback, and retry or hedge amplification

title: AI Observability and Reliability Engineering
summary: Build privacy-safe correlated telemetry, trustworthy AI service objectives, silent-fallback detection, resilience controls, and evidence-backed incident operations.
outcomes: Correlate tenant-scoped logs, metrics, traces, versions, routes, attempts, and outcomes without recording secrets or private content
Keep authoritative compliant-success, latency, error-budget, and unit-economics metrics correct under trace sampling
Detect hidden fallback and exercise circuit breakers, bulkheads, typed degradation, game days, recovery, and incident closure
Evaluate current OpenTelemetry, cloud, and AI-observability tooling against maturity, privacy, scale, operations, and exit requirements

title: AI Evaluation, Experimentation, and Causal Impact
summary: Build representative offline release evidence, calibrated human and model evaluation, and causal product experiments with explicit uncertainty and decision rights.
outcomes: Design versioned datasets, metric contracts, risk slices, paired estimates, and three-way release gates
Calibrate model judges against blinded human labels and audit disagreement, order bias, and drift
Pre-register and analyze randomized experiments with ITT, guardrails, SRM, CUPED, adoption, and heterogeneity
Reason explicitly about DAGs, confounding, mediators, colliders, propensity assumptions, and difference-in-differences

title: AI Security, Red Teaming, and Governance
summary: Threat-model the full AI system, contain fallible models with application controls, measure adversarial and benign outcomes, and govern residual risk with fresh evidence.
outcomes: Model assets, trust boundaries, injection, exfiltration, excessive agency, tool/context poisoning, supply chain, unsafe output, and resource exhaustion
Enforce tenant/resource binding, signed tool admission, egress, DLP, output safety, budgets, and exact approval outside the model
Build labelled red-team and benign suites with separate blocked-attempt, forbidden-outcome, detection, false-block, and coverage metrics
Bind inventory, threat models, control evidence, system cards, and independent expiring residual-risk acceptance into a three-way governance gate

title: CI/CD, Infrastructure, and AI DevOps
summary: Promote one immutable AI release graph through provenance, evidence, OIDC, reviewed infrastructure, progressive delivery, rollback, and recovery.
outcomes: Bind code, image, model, prompt, policy, data, evaluation, and infrastructure into a verifiable release
Use short-lived workload identity and apply only the exact reviewed infrastructure plan
Evaluate canaries, restore a known-good release, and prove recovery against RTO, RPO, integrity, and authorization
Compare current CI/CD, IaC, supply-chain, progressive-delivery, and MLOps tools

title: Solution Architecture and Technical Strategy
summary: Turn constraints into options, decisions, target architecture, and migration strategy.
outcomes: Write defensible ADRs
Evaluate build versus buy
Communicate trade-offs

title: Enterprise AI Operating Model and Leadership
summary: Create the standards, portfolio, team interactions, and narrative that scale AI delivery.
outcomes: Design decision rights
Prioritize an AI portfolio
Lead without direct authority
